prompts.abrasion_mask_v2:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: production PBR scratch/abrasion coverage data texture for a smart material. Generate a single extremely detailed 2048 by 2048 square grayscale bitmap, full canvas. This is numerical texture data, not a photograph of an object.
Primary request: physically believable wear from years of irregular mechanical contact on metal. Pure black is untouched material. Thin irregular white and gray marks are scratch coverage. 88–94 percent of pixels should remain black or almost black. Arrange fine hairline scratches into intermittent, naturally clustered drag abrasions with varied direction and pressure, tapering imperfect trajectories and overlapping fine scoring. A few longer curved scratches, short broken fine cuts, rubbed regions containing hundreds of very fine individual striations, and very sparse tiny impact nicks. Most scratches are 1–3 pixels wide at 2048px, several are 4–6 pixels wide; wide marks consist of multiple fine parallel tracks and have ragged broken boundaries. Rich variation of mark length and intensity. Local clusters show a common drag direction while other clusters point differently. Areas of undamaged black must separate the clusters.
Composition: exact flat orthographic raw mask, continuous infinite surface, seamless repeating pattern across all four borders. Edge-to-edge content, no margins, no perspective.
Color values: achromatic grayscale only, black background, different gray to white abrasion marks with sharp detailed profiles, no color tint. No shadows or light, no baked highlights, no material shading, no gradient lighting, no vignette.
Avoid: random uniformly scattered short white dashes, orderly repeated hatch marks, broad bands or zebra stripes, scratch icons, starbursts, grunge clouds, fog, object silhouettes, border, text, labels, multiple panels, spheres, renders. The pattern must read as authentic microscopic mechanical damage and look excellent close up.
prompts.brushed_relief_v2:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: production PBR microscopic height data texture for genuinely finely brushed and machined metal. Generate one extremely detailed 2048 x 2048 square grayscale bitmap. This is a material DATA map, never a lit metal photograph and never a sphere.
Primary request: an exact flat view of the subtle microscopic topography of fine longitudinal hand-brushed metal. Neutral middle gray value 128 is the level surface. Delicate dark gray 80–120 are incised hairline tool grooves; light gray 135–170 are microscopic ridge edges. Thousands of exquisitely fine, narrow, shallow, predominantly horizontal grooves with natural imperfect continuity, slight wandering, staggered ends, uneven spacing and pressure. Different lengths, widths and intensities create fine authentic brushed finish. Grooves cluster gently in small patches where the abrasive passed multiple times. Very sparse oblique hairline scratches break the direction. Barely perceptible microscopic pitting, very fine and low contrast. Nearly all lines are 1–3 pixels wide in the 2048px map; no large features. A continuous dense microstructure over the whole image. The height relief is subtle but crisp and detailed, like profilometry scan data.
Composition: flat orthographic grayscale map, a small square area of an infinite surface, seamless texture on every border, unbroken tileable grain. Edge-to-edge with no background margins. Overall tone uniform middle gray across the square.
Constraints: only grayscale values encode surface elevation; brighter means higher, darker means lower. Absolutely no broad dark or bright bands, no directional lighting, no reflections, no metallic sheen, no gradients or vignette, no spotlight. No rings, circles, zebra stripes, crosshatching, herringbone, embossed ridges, coarse corrugation, or fabric. No objects, text, labels, sphere, rendered sample, borders, multiple panels.
